subject: Decision criteria & SLA targets - follow-up (latency, cost, deployment)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Thompson <sarah.thompson@finova.com>, James Rivera <james.rivera@finova.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@finova.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + decision criteria (latency / cost / deployment)

Hi Sarah / James -

Thanks for the productive call this morning. Quick recap and a set of clarifying questions so we can align the right deployment and pricing options for Finova.

Key decision criteria we heard on the call:
- Latency targets: critical product flows need p95 <= 250-200ms for short prompts (<= 128 tokens). Non-critical batch flows can accept higher p95 (~500ms).
- Cost objective: target a ~30% reduction in per-inference unit cost vs your current provider across high-volume flows.
- Deployment mode: prefer Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) with VPC peering for predictable latency. Private (on-prem/VPC with private control plane) is an option if procurement requires full network isolation.
- SLA: finance/product expects an availability SLA in the 99.9% range and clear RPO/RTO for incidents; also need commitment around latency SLOs for dedicated capacity.
- Security/compliance: SOC 2 Type II report, customer-managed KMS integration, and audit logs are mandatory.
- Procurement timeline: target 6-8 weeks (procurement + legal).

Questions / next steps for you:
1) Can you confirm the economic buyer and final approver for the contract? (we heard it may be Sarah + Procurement.)
2) Do you have a prioritized list of the product flows (high/medium/low) so we can map cost/latency tradeoffs?
3) Any specific procurement or security documents you want up front (e.g., vendor questionnaire, SOC 2, encryption attestation)?

What we'll do on our side this week:
- Put together a Dedicated capacity sizing + pricing sketch aligned to your peak QPS and target latency.
- Run a quick benchmark with a representative prompt shape for your high-priority flows and share results (latency p50/p95, token cost estimate).
- Attach a draft Redwood Dedicated SLA and a short checklist of security artifacts.

Proposed next meeting: 30-min procurement walkthrough on Thursday or Friday this week to go over procurement steps and outstanding questions. What time works best?

Thanks again - I'll loop Rishi (pricing) and Vivek (benchmarking/runtime) to get the numbers over to you.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Marissa -

Quick pricing sketch for Finova (ballpark, subject to sizing/benchmarks):

Option A - Dedicated Reserved (recommended):
- Committed monthly: $65,000/month (includes reserved GPU pool sized for estimated peak of ~250 QPS across flows).
- Included throughput: baseline commit supports sustained throughput up to the committed QPS with autoscale headroom for burst (up to 1.5x) at overage rates.
- Per-1k-token equivalent: ~ $0.60 per 1k tokens at commit (estimate; will refine after we confirm actual token footprint).
- Discount: 10% for 12-month term; 18% for 24-month term.

Option B - Dedicated + Private Control Plane (for stricter isolation):
- Premium: +15% on committed monthly price (covers private control plane & additional compliance workflow).

Trial / procurement suggestions:
- 4-week pilot with a smaller reserved bucket ($18k) to validate latency and throughput; convert to committed once benchmarks validated.
- Include Redwood Dedicated SLA (draft attached) and SOC 2 Type II report.

I'm attaching a short one-page sketch and the draft Dedicated SLA stub. I'll iterate after Vivek shares latency numbers - we may adjust committed sizing.

'Rishi

Hi Sarah / James -

Thanks for the quick turn. Per your asks below, please find consolidated answers and next steps:

1) SLA & security artifacts
- Attached: Redwood_Dedicated_SLA.pdf (draft) and our SOC 2 Type II report (we will share via secure link to procurement).
- For Private control plane / on-prem options we can provide customer-managed KMS and extended audit logs; consider Option B if procurement requires full isolation.

2) Latency benchmarks (high-level) - Vivek's summary
- Test model family: Llama-3-70B-like (FP16/quantization-compatible execution)
- Test shape: 128-token prompts, typical response length 64 tokens
- Hardware: A100 80GB equivalent (Dedicated pool)
- Results (Dedicated reserved pool, baseline batching): p50 = 85ms, p95 = 240ms for the 128-token prompt shape at the estimated peak QPS (250). We observed tight p95 variance under steady-state; bursts can increase p95 but autoscale headroom mitigates this. Full benchmark PDF attached (redwood_benchmark_summary.pdf).

3) Pricing - Rishi's sketch
- Committed monthly (recommended): $65,000/month supporting ~250 QPS; per-1k-token estimate ~ $0.60 (subject to refinement after exact tokenization & usage profile).
- 12/24-month discounts available; pilot suggested to validate before committing.

4) Procurement questionnaire
- We will complete Finova's vendor security questionnaire and return by EOD Friday next week. Procurement: expect SOC 2 via secure link and the SLA draft attached.

Next steps / proposed timeline:
- Thu Aug 13, 10:30am PT: procurement walkthrough (30 min) - confirm?
- Pilot: 4-week reserved pilot (~$18k) if you want to validate latency & integration before a larger commit.
- Legal / Commercial: we can share a starter contract within 5 business days after procurement confirms requirements.

If this looks good I'll send a calendar invite for Thu 10:30am PT and attach the secure SOC 2 link.
